# ipforge_subnet_pool (Resource)

A named IP range (allocation pool) inside a subnet. An `ipforge_allocation` can name a pool to take its next free address from that range.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Split one subnet into per-workload ranges, then claim the next free
# address from a specific range.
data "ipforge_subnet" "servers" {
  cidr = "10.20.0.0/22"
}

resource "ipforge_subnet_pool" "linux" {
  subnet_id   = data.ipforge_subnet.servers.id
  name        = "linux"
  start_ip    = "10.20.3.1"
  end_ip      = "10.20.3.254"
  description = "Linux hosts"
}

# The allocation takes its address from the pool. Changing `pool` later
# replaces the allocation, because the old address belongs to the old range.
resource "ipforge_allocation" "web01" {
  subnet_id = data.ipforge_subnet.servers.id
  hostname  = "web01"
  pool      = ipforge_subnet_pool.linux.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `end_ip` (String) Last address of the pool (inclusive).
- `name` (String) Pool name, unique within the subnet.
- `start_ip` (String) First address of the pool.
- `subnet_id` (Number) ID of the subnet the pool belongs to. Changing it forces a new pool.

### Optional

- `description` (String)

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import by <subnet_id>/<pool_name>.
terraform import ipforge_subnet_pool.linux 3/linux
```
